headline: High-risk default data leakage and cascading error: Dify can read/write shared files and broad-network tools while ComfyUI exposes model files and offline workflows.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A direct prompt-injection bridge is not documented, but Dify can ingest uploaded knowledge-base files and ComfyUI exposes files/workflows. If operators manually pass ComfyUI outputs into Dify, attacker-controlled content could be reinterpreted as instructions. The pathway is unusual and manual, so blast radius is limited.
conditions: IF operators copy ComfyUI-generated text or metadata into Dify prompts or knowledge files
IF Dify workflows treat uploaded content as instruction-bearing rather than inert data
mitigations: Use a fixed template that strips instructions from imported content
Label ComfyUI outputs as untrusted before ingestion
Disable ad hoc copy-paste between systems
Review one sample workflow for prompt delimiters
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to imported artifacts

B_data_leakage.rationale: Dify reads filesystem content and writes uploaded knowledge-base files while also handling model-provider API keys and tool credentials; ComfyUI touches images, videos, audio, models, and workflows and can call the Comfy API. In a shared workspace, sensitive assets from ComfyUI can flow into Dify’s broader networked backend by default, creating a realistic leakage path.
conditions: IF both agents share a workspace or mounted directory
IF ComfyUI outputs are uploaded into Dify knowledge-base files or prompts
IF Dify forwards those contents to model providers or tools
mitigations: Separate storage directories for each agent
Restrict Dify uploads to non-sensitive samples
Rotate any exposed tool credentials
Audit one recent Dify run for file contents sent outbound
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent workspace isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ComfyUI is offline and does not write the filesystem, but Dify can execute shell, read/write files, spawn subprocesses, and uses shared state via the Dify server datastore. If both are pointed at the same directory or artifact store, Dify’s write and read capabilities can overwrite or consume ComfyUI assets without coordination. Uncertainty about the exact deployment should be treated conservatively.
conditions: IF both agents mount the same writable directory
IF Dify workflows modify files that ComfyUI also reads
IF no external locking or per-agent namespace is configured
mitigations: Put each agent in its own directory tree
Disable Dify writes to shared model folders
Add a manual lock step before file edits
Check for overlapping mounts in the deployment config
requires-engineering: add filesystem locking or namespace isolation

D_cascading_error.rationale: Dify is an agent/workflow platform that can act on tool outputs, while ComfyUI produces workflows, images, and model artifacts that may be treated as authoritative inputs. If Dify consumes ComfyUI outputs without verification, errors or hallucinated metadata can cascade into downstream actions or published results. The pair’s interaction is plausible in default orchestration, so the safer higher severity is warranted.
conditions: IF Dify workflow steps use ComfyUI outputs as authoritative inputs
IF no validation step checks file provenance or schema
IF downstream tools act on those outputs
mitigations: Insert a validation step before any action-taking tool
Require human review for generated artifacts
Compare outputs against expected schema or filenames
Log the exact ComfyUI artifact consumed by Dify
requires-engineering: add provenance-aware workflow gates

E_compliance.rationale: ComfyUI is documented as fully offline, while Dify handles model-provider API keys, tool credentials, and conversation logs and can send data to model providers/OpenAPI tools. If regulated content from ComfyUI is routed into Dify, retention and residency obligations can diverge even though both are open-source. The compliance risk is therefore a policy mismatch rather than a guaranteed violation.
conditions: IF regulated content from ComfyUI is uploaded into Dify
IF Dify retention or provider-routing settings are left at defaults
IF the deployment has residency or deletion obligations
mitigations: Review Dify retention settings now
Avoid uploading regulated content to Dify
Confirm provider-region settings for one workspace
Delete any test conversations containing sensitive data
requires-engineering: align retention and residency policies
